subject: Post-discovery: technical deep dive (60-90m) — scheduling and agenda

Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Jul 2025 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-discovery: technical deep dive (60-90m) — scheduling and agenda

Hi Alex — thanks again for a productive discovery call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Summary: You’re evaluating model-serving options for Cardinal’s recommendation engine; primary goals are sub-200ms tail latency for online scoring, secure multi-tenant data isolation, and predictable unit economics.
- Next step: Technical deep dive with our ML/infra engineers (60–90 minutes) to walk through architecture, performance expectations, and a short runbook for a pilot. 

Can you confirm:
1) Which of these time windows work for your team? (I included PT zones for reference)
   - Tue Jul 15 — 10:00–11:30 PT (preferred for our infra leads)
   - Wed Jul 16 — 13:00–14:30 PT
2) Who from Cardinal should join the call? (ideally: ML lead, infra/ops, security/compliance)
3) Any constraints we should prep for (air-gapped, data residency)?

I’ve attached a one-page discovery recap and a strawman agenda below. If those slots don’t work we can send a quick poll.

Attachments: Cardinal_Discovery_Recap.pdf (summary)

Strawman agenda (60–90m):
- 0–10m: intros + success criteria review
- 10–30m: current infra + model characteristics (Cardinal)
- 30–60m: Redwood architecture fit, latency/cost tradeoffs, dedicated vs private options
- 60–80m: runbook / pilot plan and data handling (KV cache, batching, quantization)
- 80–90m: open Q&A and next steps

If you confirm a slot I’ll loop in Ben (solutions) and Marissa (scheduling) to lock a calendar invite and prep notes for the engineers.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0183
